title: Why Is Brazil's Corinthians Named After an English Team?
description:
Corinthians, one of Brazil's biggest football clubs, is in the news this week. But its name isn't Brazilian: it was borrowed from a team of English amateur gentlemen who toured Brazil in 1910, and five São Paulo railway workers who watched them play.

🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:00 Corinthians in the news
0:04 An English name
0:09 Corinthian Football Club, London, 1882
0:13 Amateurs who were England
0:20 On tour around the world
0:22 August 1910: Brazil
0:25 10-1 over Fluminense
0:28 Six games, six wins, 38 goals
0:31 Five railway workers in São Paulo
0:35 1 September 1910: a new club
0:39 The lamp and the name
0:45 "A team of the people"
0:49 2012: club world champions
0:53 The final

A note on the story: the club dates its founding to the night of 1 September 1910 in Bom Retiro, São Paulo, after the founders watched Corinthian FC beat AA Palmeiras on 31 August. The meeting "under a lamp" is the club's own founding story, so the video calls it club lore. The 1910 tour results (six wins, 38 goals for, 6 against) are from RSSSF and Corinthian-Casuals' tour records; the two sources name the last two São Paulo opponents differently but agree on the scores.

Images: Corinthians team of 1914 and Fluminense team of 1906 (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Corinthian F.C. team, 1901 (print and cut-out), from B. O. Corbett, "Annals of the Corinthian Football Club" (Longmans, Green, 1906), via the Internet Archive. Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) outlines.
Sources: B. O. Corbett, "Annals of the Corinthian Football Club" (1906); RSSSF, "Brazilian Trip of Corinthian FC (England) 1910"; Corinthian-Casuals FC, "Corinthian Tours"; Wikipedia, "History of SC Corinthians Paulista" and "2012 FIFA Club World Cup final".
Narration voice is synthetic.
